means: The main context line of a session; during a stem it holds only the stem's handle and step lines.
A branch (git plus context) taken at the goal's turn; work runs there and folds back to the core line.
The turn where a stem branches; a cache checkpoint can sit there (stem anchor).
The stem's result re-pointed into the core line's handle once the stem finishes.
An opaque id whose bytes stay fixed in the cached prefix while what it resolves to changes.
Change what a handle resolves to in the store without editing the context bytes.
Read what a handle currently holds, with the read tool the model already uses.
Model asks for what it needs by handle, instead of the harness pushing a narrative.
A cache breakpoint chosen where it pays: system, tail or stem anchor kind.
A named versioned spec the turn loop reads at fixed seams, id strat-<name>-<major>.<minor>.
A module boundary where behavior plugs in: tools, providers, strategies, hooks, policies, handles, checkpoints, machine, coord.
A small model that checks each completed tool call and answers ok or FLAG with a reason.
A watcher note on a tool call, stored on the session (s.flags) and counted as a smell.
An operator's assessment of a session against its goal, stored as s.watched.
A Claude Code session that drives harness sessions through scripts/wh.mjs and reports what it cannot resolve.
A point before each model request or tool call where a session can be held.
State of a session waiting at a gate until step or resume.
One lockstep advance: every waiting session takes one step and holds again.
Stop every tab at its next gate; used for lockstep and for updates.
A turn spent to inspect a wait point; a passing check needs no wake.
Re-pointing what handles resolve to so a stem's downstream turns see altered or materialized context.
Write real turn content into the context where a handle stood.
The component that decides what a handle resolves to; the micro resolver is a small model doing so at the leading edge.
Models consult at checkpoints: A ahead, B look-back, plus a consult; arranged as a graph.
A generic prompt turn with a throwaway reply that registers the cache for a byte-stable payload.
A tracked issue (labels concern, kind:*, ci-failure, triaged, needs-*) worked in the background loop.
A recorded oddity (wh:smells: kind, tool, detail, steer fingerprint) tracked over time.
The generic points and directions given to a session; logged in the log repo.
Per-turn session rows: prompt, cached, cacheWrite, completion, reasoning, cost, bp kinds, strat id, upstream.
A live value drawn by CSS from data-v via slot(el, value); changes without re-rendering.
A named CSS rule via rule(name, css); UI state is a rule, not a node edit.
Checks written from the goal and committed red before the implementation.
A check fails (red) before implementation and passes (green) after.
A measured comparison against plain serial turns, run with scripts/casestudy.mjs.
The baseline: plain serial turns without stems; results are reported relative to it.
The provider route behind a model on OpenRouter; stems inherit the core's upstream so the cache holds.
The shared in-browser VM and its host, with per-session unix users.
A set of sessions sharing a profile (settings such as strategy and watchModel).
A redaction handle form: what it resolves to is hidden from the model.
A registered function on the terminal path, direction up or down, that sanitizes or alters text; register(dir, name, label, fn).
A rule in app/policy.js that decides whether a tool call or write is allowed or needs approval.
Text cut short on screen that shows whole on hover or press-and-hold, from data-full or a slot's data-v.
A segmented page element built once by item() or R.part(); segments are filled, the card is never rebuilt.
Render rule: a node is created once and never rebuilt; state shows through slots and rules.
The in-page dialog modal({title, body, actions}) that replaces alert, confirm and prompt.
An edit panel on a row with discard, keep editing or save, shown from and to values.
How a model steers its own work unaided; observed before any structure is added.
Fixing a workflow as explicit steps in the prompt, compared against natural steering and altered or materialized turns.
A second model, given procedures and background, swaps or alters turns or the flow of the first model's session.
A strategy that applies only where a condition holds, such as a long core; its own id, compared with serial.
A real development session driven as a person drives it through scripts/wh.mjs; never a puzzle or challenge prompt.
The test-only provider with a modelled prefix cache; proves mechanics, not model behaviour.
A per-agent append-only file catalog/inbox/<agent>-<shortid>.jsonl that only the steward merges into the catalog.
The eight steps every piece of work follows, from naming it to release, with fixed owners.
After a group of turns, send the context plus a marker, ask for one word, discard the reply; the product is a cache entry.
Markers like [label, tag, tag] in the cached prefix that later resolvers give meaning to, instead of a concrete steer baked into cached bytes.
A judged payload of past turns plus an instruction naming the action; the model commits to one line; dropped after a few light turns.
A small model builds a payload from data, not content (under 10k tokens); a frontier model then operates on it.
Helper work is capped by max_tokens, a payload budget and a ledger row per operation, with a smell over the cap.
One harness-added request: watch, helper, steward, probe, nudge, graft, recraft or confer; cost taken from its ledger row.
A helper rewrites one wordy reasoning block, dropping loops and never renaming a name; the raw text stays in the log behind a handle.
Named voices with structure, before/after and degree of coherence, chosen by strategy policy.
Marking terms as crafted, proper, label or regular: a deterministic first pass, then a zero-shot pass that only proposes.
One per-instance markdown file read by helper workers as a cached prefix; workers carry no context between items.
One experiment's two arms, blue (current plus exact brief) and green (candidate), each with its own session, strategy id and throwaway branch.
The first silo stage: one task, one run per arm, hard cost cap; stop if green costs over 2x blue or is unreviewable.
A Fable subagent run in Claude Code, not the API, that proposes falsifiable hypotheses and never touches a branch.
The manual baseline: name files and lines, copy find strings from what was just read, one file per commit, stop at the approval card.
Steering that comes from the strategy (system-prompt base plus hooked turn wrappers), versioned with the strategy id; a hand nudge is a missing directive.
Any wh say after the first message that is not an approval answer; counted from the wh log, target 0 for green.
Tool results byte-identical to an earlier result of the same tool in the session, over all tool calls.
Metadata-only profile of every session's turns, with a drill by index into content only where a number points; descriptive, never a verdict.
Dark, light and system modes as named CSS custom properties that developers can override.
Cost, tokens, cache, calls and checkpoints as widgets the user places in named slots; developers register widgets.
Per-part templates and an ordered text-transform pipeline with sanitized inline markup, so turn appearance is open to developers.
A stored, ordered sequence of turns (a conversation track) from a catalog; applied at bootstrap or mid-session.
The set of flows plus the approaches that allocate their turns, with what each policy, trigger and resolution aimed for.
A cheap helper model that picks which flow starts or joins a conversation, before any provider API is called.
An attributable label on a turn or flow, kept beside the turns; means anything; tags and flows are many-to-many.
A change of a conversation's tag set along the way; the first set is the tag pivot.
A rule binding a tag set to a flow with a trigger, an aim and a per-strategy awareness setting.
A turn with typed fields (voice, content, context values) and a validation shape, holding no fixed wording.
The typed parameters of a turn template; not a UI slot (see slot).
An advanced pre-allocated stack of templated turns, filled by helpers, heuristics or both.
Like a turn stack but dispersed through the conversation, allocation guaranteed by policy.
A check extracted from one step bullet or directive of a skill or agent md file, run as a flow's turns resolve steps.
Analytics over tags, flows, validations and costs that assess the flow approach itself: quality gained and tokens saved against baselines.
Cheap helper or logic that picks a flow per case against a route rubric, pre-provider, any provider; records confidence per pick.
Pre-allocated templated turns, e.g. spun up to meet a provider cache size floor before the flow is sent.
Templated turns dispersed through the conversation, allocation guaranteed by policy; saturated dithering is so dense it looks serial.
A check from one step bullet of a skill or agent md file; never blocks, it carries issues and tags to flows.
Timestamped, session and flow-state attributed data, never rewritten, queried to find successes, issues and further strategies.
The labels and directive saying when a flow should be routed a given way; the router is judged against it.
The stated starting basis of a tag set; easy to gauge, record and verify beside the turns.
Where tags are made and documented in flight, then asserted after the fact.
A trial of a pitched tag with its hypothesis, using all existing conventions, before the flow relies on it.
Changing a flow's protocol mid-flow when it shows more issues than anticipated; the flow then continues.
One tagged policy's thread through the chronological turn state; strands pick up and fall off interleaved.
The strands of all active tagged policies together, across flows.
Resolves what falls outside the scope of the tagged policies so the strand meets back into scope.
One policy tag's run along the turn state; strides of several policies pass each other.
Turn dithering so dense that the conversation looks serial.
A terse cached context a hot agent works from.
An active agent that produces or guides turns from baked templates off a context pin.
A small API call tapped against a hot agent's delegator state; many do much of the heavy lifting.
A policy seam's parameters and its return payload shape.
The policy tags in force plus where each flow's turns stand, with open concerns, at a turn, attributed to session and flow.
From a state, a condition selects the transition expected next; recorded with its source and confidence.
The point where a state moves to its next state; not the halt/step gate of coord.js (see gate).
Accumulated open concerns in a state, worked like a for-loop or queue, strapped or naturally.
A policy-chosen model that sees only semantic entries and picks which turns to stack next.
A high-level item (semantics plus contextual information and data) associated with which turns to stack next.
How a concern queue is worked, strapped or natural; the amount of influence is a recorded choice.
Influence mode where policy straps a dithered stack of turns on to steer a concern queue.
Shaping flows from state and policy first, stitched imperatively and declaratively, with handlers choosing turns without seeing them.
A change of the tag set along the way; one input to a state's move at a transition gate.
Timestamped, state-attributed data, never rewritten, queried as: given this state, projected transition versus the one that occurred.
The enumerated blobs of a development target with metadata and captures; harness data beside the turns.
One blob by label with its kind, data domain, metadata and captures.
A high-level extract of an entry (signatures, test names, headers); never stands in for content not read.
A catalogued way to capture (ast, regex, parser, metadata, iac); combinations are catalogued and built upon.
The synopsis of what can be queried over an inventory, and which fields come back.
What a session read of an entry (whole, slice or capture only), and when.
Derived from entries and check records: per entry what is held and what was actually checked.
The kind of content an entry holds: code language, spreadsheet, essay, image, network config.
An inventory over IaC or captured datapoints such as IPs, subnets and allow and deny lists.
A language service (as in VS Code) exposing symbols, definitions, references and types as a materialized reference; a capture source (how: lsp).
An inventory entry for one symbol: name, kind, container, file, range, signature, references count.
A link between two symbols (call, import, extends, reads, writes) from a language service.
The agent choosing which symbols or seams it wants to edit, with why given as a semantic entry.
An edit naming a symbol or node path and an operation, never a text position found by searching.
Here: regenerating files from an altered AST graph; the output is a normal diff under the usual approval.
Anything meeting the capture seam contract: returns symbol entries and reference edges, applies structural edits, returns a codegen result; one per language.
A comment or note attached to a node path or concern in the graph, outside files; kind note, doc or functional.
A comment that changes behaviour or legal standing if removed (license header, shebang, tool directive); survives codegen verbatim.
The address of a node in a language's own AST or node graph; a structural edit names one.
The record of one step validator resolved against one session: pass, fail or unresolved, with a pointer to the evidence; never blocking.
Where a session's shell tool runs: the in-browser machine, or a host exec target. Setting shellOn (defaults, profile, session).
A named place the local bridge runs commands in: a launcher, a user and a directory fixed by the person's --exec flag.
How the bridge reaches an exec target's bash: local, wsl, podman, docker, wsl-podman, wsl-docker; one small table entry each.
The shell tool's runner that sends each command to an exec target through the local bridge; same tool definition and result shape.
The documented list of words that would tell a model what runs it; no text the harness gives a model may contain one.
JSONL file wh appends per command: time, command, session id, outcome, sizes and hashes; never message text or keys.
Why a run ended, recorded by the harness in session.stops with the log length: done, limit, failed, stopped, held or budget.
An operator message sent right after a run stopped at the tool-round limit; counted apart from steering nudges.
A steering wh say after the first message: not an approval answer, not a limit continuation; counted from the operator log, target 0 for green.

A read that names its range (lines a-b, or offset and length in characters) and gets that range back whole up to a stated cap, with a last line naming what was left out; set per strategy by reads: ranged.

Per tool call, its arguments with place and command fields kept as written (path, op, ref, branch, lines, handle, a command line) and content fields replaced by {length, hash}; keys masked; no turn text, no file content.
The identity of a file's content: contentHash over its text with CRLF as LF (binary raw); equal checksums are one thing whatever the labels.
Derived from entries and check records: what is held and what was checked, per entry or joined per checksum with all labels.
A read naming its range, returned whole up to a cap; a last line names what was left out. Strategy setting reads: ranged.
Per tool call, its arguments: place and command fields as written, content fields as length and hash only, keys masked.
Ledger field on a request row: how many times the provider seam asked again after a transient failure before the first chunk. Absent when 0; never sent to the model.
A short operator message sent right after a run stopped as failed (for example HTTP 502); counted apart from steering in the turn profile.
Ledger field on a main request row: times the provider seam asked again after a transient failure before the first chunk; absent when 0.
A short operator message sent right after a run stopped as failed; counted apart from steering in the turn profile.
Turn-profile count: tool calls before the first shell call whose kept command line runs git commit; null when none.
The documented words that would tell a model what runs it; under strat-serial-3.0 no text the harness gives a model contains one.
Strategy field wording: absent sends descriptions and helper lines as first registered; neutral (strat-serial-3.0) names nothing of what runs the tools.
Setting hostFiles: a session whose shell runs on a host also gets file_read, file_edit and file_write there, through the exec route.
Setting toolRounds: model-tool round trips in one user turn before the turn stops as limit; default 8 (MAX_STEPS), branches keep 8.
What a shell or local tool tells the model when it fails. Neutral under strat-serial-3.0; strategies registered before it keep the texts they read.
A step validator pattern of kind template that matches only at the start of an argument (a Spec: label); also read against commit messages.
A tool call whose long arguments sit in the output store under a handle; the log keeps {ref, name, want} and an argument summary.
What a held tool call's card and wh held show: the tool name and its arguments, resolved from the handle for a stored call.
A shell call whose command line writes a file by script: inline python or node, a here-document, sed -i, or a redirect or tee.
Field x.held on a tool message, set by the harness when the call waited at a hold; the turn profile counts held calls from it.
State of a held tool-call card whose arguments are a handle alone (data-ref): stored, unknown, lost or other.
One scripted command that gathers what a step needs from the host in a single call, replacing many model exploring turns.
The host is data and a command asks it a question; the model gets the answer, not the path of exploring it.
The model states intent in words; policy tags pick a fixed command, so the model generates no parameters.
How a command's output is trimmed and formatted, set by command type and its single-purpose params; names before metadata.
A terse label a small model says in place of a command; the alias carries the params and the tidy-up.
A keyed holder of a deferred result: a fixed query collects the state of an undetermined target; a goal fans out into buckets.
A turn pre-filled as slot-like sentences bound to labels and data, so a router picks references by fuzzy position; fields, not UI slots.
An external label on an item picked or important, kept beside the turns; the most recent label picks the variant.
Who may call a helper: only the harness (depth one); a helper never drives another helper.
Each step goes to the cheapest actor able to do it: code, then query, then small model, then the main model.
How much aid (aliases, routes, partial turns, markers) a session gets; set per model and recorded, like influence mode.
The app platform: a wasm-native, protocol-first, time-positional runtime for apps with V8-and-HTML-class capability. Hypothesis; not built.
An interface point of one feature, stated as data: operations, typed payloads, timestamps, errors. Components bind to it directly. Cf seam contract.
The smallest set of platform contracts the design starts from (clock, stream, store, surface, module, identity); each addition is named with its cost.
A wasm component reaching a contract through the platform's own call surface, with no JavaScript layer between them.
A unit of wasm code that uses and implements platform contracts and nothing else; the platform's unit of app code.
Rule that every exchange of the app names a platform protocol from the catalog; there is no ambient request API.
Fetching a page as data over a named protocol; one capability among others, not the app's entry point or shell.
A named, versioned exchange rule held in the protocol catalog (transport, security, exchange, cache, regulatory). Not docs/PROTOCOL.md, the harness protocol.
Data set of platform protocol records the platform reads; pluggable by adding records; holds the defaults. No protocol is named in code.
The kind of a platform protocol record: transport, security, exchange, cache or regulatory; an exchange names at most one protocol per layer.
The record used for a layer when an exchange omits it; picked by default marks in catalog data, never by a code constant.
Partial cache invalidation by listing the members to drop (ids or a result-set enumeration), instead of whole-cache or time-only expiry.
A query result whose members can be listed by stable id with count and cursor, so cache entries and invalidation address members.
A protocol record of layer regulatory: a privacy law or data-security rule (GDPR, US rules) applied as checks on exchanges; swapped by data.
A protocol record of layer security: TLS version, key exchange and signature suites including post-quantum, and certificate authority handling.
The user the app acts for; the app holds the principal's authority only through delegations.
A scoped, revocable grant by which the app acts for its principal; every outward effect names the delegation it uses.
Anything the app reads that it did not author: network bytes, files, pages, model output, other components. Data, never instruction.
Source, protocol and time attached to each ingested datum; trust decisions read it instead of an origin name.
The link between the app's view and its server; its encryption is set up from the security suite with no app code or user step.
An input or event as one immutable record: start time, event transitions with times, payload, source.
A timed change inside one event record (for example down, move, up). Not a tag transition or transition gate of flows.
State kept as timestamped versions so a handler can read it as it stood at a given time.
Reading state as it stood at a given timestamp, not as it is now; the only read a platform handler gets.
Event records ordered by timestamp, consumed against intervals; scheduling is comparing record timestamps with now.
Catalog data stating unit, clock, epoch origin and tie order for timestamps; read by the platform, not a constant.
Fixing an interval's boundaries at floor(epoch / n) * n so ticks of all scheduled functions fall on one shared grid.
The scheduling test: an item is due when its timestamp is at or before the queue's now; comparison only, no timers.
A function run for one given timestamp that reads state as-of it; no schedule; replayable from the timeline.
A function run by the queue at epoch-pinned ticks; each run leaves a run trace.
The record of one function run: input timestamps, as-of reads, outputs and guard verdicts.
A predicate over a trace projection; when it fails, runs depending on that run are knocked out. Not the flow guard (xblxxs).
The fields and timestamps of a run trace that one trace guard looks at; a view, not a copy. Not flow projection (gwokxx).
Voiding the runs that depend on a run whose trace guard failed: not run if pending, marked void if already run.
The platform's styling and drawing: CSS-like style rules as data plus shader specs, applied to surface nodes.
The drawable area and node tree of an app, reached through the surface contract; look applies to it.
A contract-stated description of a GPU program: stages, bindings, entry points; written against the graphics baseline.
The GPU API the browser community settled on (WebGPU or its successor over WebGL), recorded as data with evidence and date.
One line of the explored catalog: a source looked at for a concern, with date, kept blob, its location, unread ranges and breadcrumbs.
The smallest excerpt or own-words summary of a source that answers the concern; noise (nav, ads, boilerplate, changelogs) filtered out. Not the skill blob (C10).
A part of a source the pass did not read (sections, line or character ranges, linked pages), recorded so a later run can resume there.
A deferred pointer to a resource seen or inferred but not followed, tied to its source blob, with a confidence and the reason it waits.
How a claim is known: concrete (read and checked), gist (seen in a summary), inferred (from memory or context; confirming search deferred).
The order concerns are explored in a coarse run: function and features, then security, then nomenclature and its meaning for the product. Lower ranks wait.
A survey pass with a source budget per concern (default 5): search first, the one best source, smallest blob kept, the rest left as breadcrumbs.
A re-run whose result equals the previous result does not invalidate its dependents; they are not re-run. Prior art in build systems and incremental compilers.
Per-trigger rule for ticks missed while a scheduler was down or busy: fire once now, skip to the next tick, or fire all. Same shape as the catch-up policy in time.md.
Candidate GPU API a shader spec targets (WebGPU, or successor over WebGL); a record with date and evidence docs/platform/survey-A6-A7.md S7.1, 2026-11-21. 'Settled' unproven.
Scoped, revocable grant the app acts under for its principal; effects name it. Any gate, allowlist or deny rule is an option, off by default.
Per-trigger rule for ticks missed while a scheduler was down or busy: fire once now, skip to next tick, or fire all missed.
A name borrowed from an everyday thing for a data class; the thing named is data, classed by semantics and read forward-causally.
A data class: what a step needs from a host, gathered in one call instead of exploring turns; analogy name, host kind left open.
A data class: the result of a fixed query, keyed and deferred; a goal fans out into buckets. Analogy name, store left open.
A data class: a turn pre-filled as sentences with labeled, data-bound parts, so a router picks references by fuzzy position; analogy name.
A data class: a label beside the turns on a picked or important item; the most recent label picks the variant. Analogy name.
Threat model: a recursively self-improving agent with strong cryptographic solving and exploiting ability that breaks or exploits any single weak control easily.
Protocol record of layer security: TLS version, key exchange and signature suites including post-quantum, CA handling; designed against an RSI-grade adversary (hnqzly).
Voiding in-app derived state of runs depending on a run whose trace guard failed: not run if pending, void if run. Not external effects.
Survey pass with a budget of 3 sources per area; fetched or searched, each counts. Search first, keep the smallest blob, defer the rest.
A pluggable provider path that serves harness turns through Claude, behind the existing provider seam, beside OpenRouter.
A local proxy between the real Claude Code and the API that applies policy to request and stream and forwards credential headers untouched.
A pure function called at each stream event boundary that returns pass, halt or alter, checked progressively against a budget.
The property that code in the route copies credential headers without reading, logging or storing them; checked by a canary scan.
Per-event stream function returning pass, halt or alter against a budget; ends one response stream. Unlike 'halt' (qofxtx), which stops every tab.
Stock Claude Code TUI in tmux session claude inside a WSL distro, signed in by the user, as the base for live route checks.
Lossy, policy-driven reduction of a text blob to a skeleton of kept spans and omission markers; pure function, full blob stays behind its handle.
The output of striping: one header line, then kept spans interleaved with omission markers, parseable back to source offsets.
A substring of the source retained verbatim in a skeleton; never adjacent to another kept span, never empty.
Single-line placeholder [~N,wW,lL,kX] for an omitted run: UTF-16 unit count, then words, newlines, kind sketch above a size threshold.
Marker detail k: letters, digits, punctuation, whitespace-only or mixed, by share of non-space chars in the omitted run.
Plain object choosing mode, budget, protect patterns, keep-first/last, class override and known terms; every key optional, restrictions off by default.
Pure function (text, policy) to shorter text with a header; squeeze, keyword lines, head and tail, and striping are all reducers.
Versioned name of one reducer behaviour, such as stripe-1.0; a changed byte is a new id and ids are never reused.
Notional label in the skeleton header, derived from line features (list, headed, json, code, log, tabular, prose, mixed), selecting the cue profile.
Weight of a unit by how few segments hold it, whole blob and local window, in smoothed df arithmetic (Zipf and IDF-shaped).
Header suffix seen[ PCT%] telling the model this blob was already reduced, with the same policy (header only) or another cut.
Smallest run a skeleton may keep: 2 chars, 3 once its adjacent delimiter is attached; shorter unprotected runs are dropped.
Kept source units over source length, reported as pct in the header; distinct from the output-length budget, which counts header and markers.
Monotone post-selection pass: attach adjacent delimiters, fill gaps under minGap, drop short kept runs; makes retained sets nest as budget grows.
Standalone module and tool contract: an agent fetches harness data with a small GraphQL-subset query and may act only on what the result declares.
Block returned first with every query result: flattened, deduped decorator attributes, kinds, labels, declared interactions and the reducer applied.
A directive on a query or field whose defaulted attributes (reducer, descriptor, limits, interactions) merge into the header; policy can change the defaults.
Class of a result set's entries; states which interactions its labels support and the function that fetches an entry's payload or top-level properties.
Name of a node or value among a result set's entries; the only thing query-ref may address. Not the passive marker.
Call on a label from an earlier query: get, set or property. Refused unless that query declared the interaction for that label.
An interaction (get, set, property) a query lists in its header for a label; every query-ref must match one.
The query's shape implies follow-up interactions; the surface infers them and lists them in the header, so the model need not guess.
The point where a policy-chosen reducer is applied to a payload; the header names the reducer applied. Sibling of text striping.
Kind whose entries are produced from data on request; an automatic syntax descriptor is appended unless a preface flag drops it.
Interface (schema, resolve, label, get/set) through which the query layer reads and writes one source; the harness adapter comes first.
The extent in which a query's labels and declared interactions are valid; a label outside its scope is refused and expires with the query.
Long arc of 6 to 12 stories toward one capability, on real artefacts with pre-registered measures; each story is one pass of the rigid order.
Which harness runs a story sessions: 0 cheap-model WebHarness, 1 with query surface and striping, 2 Claude Code through the gateway.
Recorded check (G0, G1, G2, GB, GJ) that must exist before a driver stage or story group opens; met by records, not dates.
Platform host that embeds its own wasm engine and binds every contract natively, so no JavaScript value crosses a contract call.
Platform realised as a layer over a browser engine; wasm components run there and contracts bind through JavaScript glue at the edge.
The set of wasm features and binding conventions a contract binding may assume of a guest and its engine.
Paper check naming which contract operations carry each field of a real harness record shape, or recording a shape gap.
A field or behaviour of a real record shape no contract operation carries; written as a hypothesis with its cost, not as a new contract.
The option picked provisionally from the project md files with its reason and a flip condition; a hypothesis, not a decision.
Span of a result label's validity: begins at the result's as-of time, ends at exactly one terminator from a closed catalog-held set.
A label resolves only against the result whose header declared it; aliases are platform-issued, so content-derived strings mint no ref.
What a reduced view may assert: existence, position and omitted counts as of its time; never absence, completeness, equivalence or safety.

Instance of query scope (sibling nomenclature mutcns, aka ref scope; docs/QUERY.md#44-scope-and-expiry): a label is addressable only as <result>/<label> against its own result. Platform adds: the pair is validated against the declaration record, and a string spelled in ingested content mints nothing.

Extension of label lifetime (docs/QUERY.md 4.4 @scope: queries N, ticks N, surface): the platform adds a closed terminator set held as catalog data (completed, invalidated, superseded, expired on an epoch grid, epoch-fold, revoked) and as-of replay of get after termination.
Instance of query scope (mutcns): a label resolves only as <result>/<label> against its own result; the pair is checked against the declaration record.
see: docs/platform/query-surface.md (P-Q1); docs/QUERY.md#44-scope-and-expiry. A string spelled in ingested content mints no label.

means: Extension of label lifetime (QUERY.md 4.4): ends at one terminator from a closed catalog-held set; get replays as-of after termination.
see: docs/platform/query-surface.md (P-Q2); terminators: completed, invalidated, superseded, expired on an epoch grid, epoch-fold, revoked.

means: The route a large result takes from its source to the model: handle and view, ranged reads, query and query_ref, reducers such as striping.
Strategy strat-query-1.0: strat-stem-1.0 plus the query and query_ref tools and the result header; a striping arm gets its own id, never an edit.
Questions with known answers over this repo's own ledgers, profiles and catalog, each answer computed by script without a model, fixed before any run.
Kind of read task: lookup of an extreme or single record, aggregation across many records, or locate then act on one part.
A corpus question whose final answer equals the computed expectation under the scoring rule written before the run; the model's own claim does not count.
Prompt plus completion tokens from a session's ledger, summed over its requests, per solved task; unsolved runs are reported apart, never averaged in.
What one experiment arm could read of the data and of the other arm, written down per arm as PROGRAMME isolation requires.
First solve rate and cost of the cheap non-Anthropic models on the read-path corpus under strat-stem-1.0; the reference for later A1 arms.
A query tool's return: header on line 1, then body JSON; a large body sits behind an os: handle, the header never cut.
Checks joining the query surface to tools, strategies, handles, ledger and the stripe hook; ci key queryint, red until A1.3.
Contract checks for stripe-1.0 named by @reduce at the query surface, wherever the registry lives; ci key querystripe, red until A1.4.
